transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes — clean the pump filter first. A hot or slightly burning smell during drying is often fluff collecting in the drying/drain path and getting overheated; restricted airflow can also make drying very slow. Switch the machine off, unplug it and let it cool, then put towels and a shallow tray at the lower-front filter flap, loosen the filter slowly, remove fluff/debris and refit it securely. Also make sure the cold-water tap is on, the drain hose is not kinked, and try drying only about half a normal wash load, as washer-dryers cannot usually dry a full wash load. If the smell is strong, acrid, smoky, or continues after cleaning, stop using the drying function and arrange an engineer visit rather than running it again.

Ok. The smell is like burning dust or scorched fabric, and the top of the machine feels very hot to touch when it's drying. I've been carrying on using it though. I usually dry a full 8-9kg wash load straight after washing.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Do not use the drying function again, even with a smaller load, until it has been checked by a qualified appliance engineer. The main possibilities are lint/fluff restricting the drying/condensing path and overheating, or a fault with the drying heater, thermostat or fan; the very hot top makes an overheating fault a real concern. With it unplugged and completely cool, the only useful owner check is the lower-front pump filter: use towels and a shallow tray, open it slowly, and remove any fluff or debris.

candidates: Fluff/lint restriction in the drying airflow or drain path (high)
Drying load too large or unsuitable drying setting (medium)
Drying heater, thermostat or fan fault (low)
